name: A solution
description: one medium, buffer or stock solution as the bench makes it — what goes in, how much, at what final volume, and the procedure that is the part people actually get wrong
phrases: the shape of a solution recipe

solution.description: the lab's name for it, as written on the bottle. Underscores and hyphens are both in use and mean nothing — trace_metal_soln and trace-vitamin-soln sit in the same folder

description.description: what it is for, in the words that will make sense a year later

volume.description: the final volume the composition below makes, IN LITRES. It is the denominator every amount is relative to, so a composition without it cannot be scaled and must be used exactly as written

source.description: where this recipe was read from, named well enough for somebody to go back to it. Not a path into this repository — these recipes were written elsewhere and copied here

composition.description: what goes in. ORDER IS THE ORDER OF ADDITION where it matters and incidental where it does not, and the file cannot tell you which — the procedure can

name.description: the ingredient. May name another solution, which is how media compose: ABm6 takes trace_metal_soln, coli_flask_medium_v1 takes both that and 5x-ammonium-phosphate-salts

amt.description: the quantity, as written. Kept as a string because these files carry it as written and a reader must not silently reinterpret 0.1 as 0.100

units.description: g, mg, mL or uL. MASSES AND VOLUMES SIT IN THE SAME COLUMN and that is the whole reason a solution is not a `Recipe`: models/recipe.js carries only volume_uL, because it describes how one reaction is assembled, not how a medium is made

note.description: anything true of this ingredient alone — what it predissolves in, what it does not dissolve in, what the final concentration works out to

procedure.description: free prose, and the most valuable part of the record. THE ARITHMETIC IS RARELY WHAT GOES WRONG; the order, the pH and the sterilization are. The trace vitamin solution's procedure is the case for this field existing — it records that the biotin came from capsules with a cellulose carrier that never dissolved, which no composition table could express and which anybody repeating it needs to know. DOES NOT SCALE: it is prose, and a tool that multiplied '800 uL of 0.5 N NaOH' by four would be inventing a protocol

notes:
THE SERIALISATION IS THE `>field` / `>>block` DIALECT this toolkit already parses for inventory, and it was not invented for this schema. Every file under src/labplanner/data/solutions was written in it, by this lab, in the private 20n/pipeline repo — `>solution`, `>volume`, then `>>composition` with an `amt`/`units`/`note` header and `>>procedure` as prose. The schema was written afterwards, from the files.

A SOLUTION IS NOT A `Recipe`. The two were nearly merged. `models/recipe.js` states its own scope — "how individual reactions are assembled" — and its components carry `volume_uL` against an operation of PCR, Digest or Gibson. A medium's ingredients are mostly masses, so merging them would have meant writing grams into a field named volume_uL. The shape generalises; the units do not.

EVERY SOURCE FILE IS CR-ONLY. All seven that came from 20n/pipeline use classic-Mac line endings, so a reader splitting on \n alone sees each entire file as one line and finds no composition. That is not a quirk to tolerate quietly: it is how ABm6's `trace salts` ingredient read as undefined for years — searched for under every spelling of "trace salt" across a whole repository and legitimately absent, because its name is trace_metal_soln and its home is another repository entirely.

SOLUTIONS COMPOSE, AND THE SCHEMA DOES NOT ENFORCE IT. A composition line may name another solution. Nothing here checks that the named one exists, because these files are a copied historical record and a validator that refused an unresolvable name would reject the record rather than the gap.
